solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One way to kick the habit by wrapping kicking strap round compiler's middle

definitions.text: One way to kick the habit

indicators.note: wrapping means the sailing word goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a kicking strap on a sailing boat is a vang, the rope that holds the boom down

indicators.note: round joins with wrapping: the strap goes round the compiler's centre
the middle of the word compiler is its two central letters

explanation.surface: Advice on quitting smoking that somehow involves a strap tied round the crossword setter's waist.
explanation.walkthrough: The compiler's middle is the centre pair of 'compiler', PI, wrapped by VANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Switching to e-cigarettes is a common method smokers use to give up tobacco.

clue.text: Six normally start off, as far as one can see

definitions.text: as far as one can see

parts.note: six in Roman numerals is VI

indicators.note: start off says the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: normally means usually

explanation.surface: Six people who usually set off together, judging by appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' removes the U at the front of USUALLY, leaving SUALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something judged by sight alone is judged by eye, as far as appearances go.

clue.text: Even bits of toilet are seen in prestige production film

indicators.note: seen in says the toilet letters appear inside the reworked letters
a production of something remakes it, so these letters are rearranged
even bits are the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A lavatory scene turns up in a prestigious film production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is the whole definition: this is the title of a 1982 horror movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Poltergeist is a 1982 horror movie about a haunted suburban house.

clue.text: Kiss frequently and try to seduce in dilapidated shed area

parts.note: to kiss and cuddle is to neck
oft is an old word for often, frequently

indicators.note: in says the courting word sits inside the reworked shed
a dilapidated shed is broken down, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to woo someone is to court them, try to win them

explanation.surface: A couple keep kissing and courting inside a tumbledown garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilapidated' rearranges SHED as HEDS, and 'in' sets the courting word between the E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means one's local district or part of the world, a region.

clue.text: One travels to work, avoiding a true disaster

indicators.note: avoiding means the punctuation word goes without the letter a

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is a comma

indicators.note: a disaster is a wreck, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A worker on the way in avoids a genuine catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'work' is a clue piece in its own right, a rare trick. 'disaster' rearranges the four letters of 'true' as UTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone making a regular daily journey to their job is a daily traveller of this kind.

clue.text: Oscar coordinates fool's original copy?

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
x and y are the coordinates on a graph
a fool is a moron; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winning director's coordinates and a fool's original copy of a script.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase joining contradictory terms, like 'original copy', is an example of this figure of speech.

clue.text: Nice terms negotiated with yacht club

indicators.note: terms that are negotiated get reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deal struck on good terms in Nice with the local yacht club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city; it is just five letters of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an English Premier League football team, a sporting side based in the north-west.

clue.text: Links with Bangkok hotels may be on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand, so its things are Thai; inns are small hotels

explanation.surface: Links to Bangkok hotels could be broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thai inns', said out loud, gives the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-ins are connections, especially promotional products linked to a film or show.

clue.text: Explores Istanbul's stonewall

indicators.note: the 's reads as has: the two words have the answer inside them, across the join

explanation.surface: Someone touring Istanbul's famous old walls.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate signal word: the letters run across 'exploRES ISTanbul'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to block or hold out against something, to refuse to give way.

clue.text: Speak outright

definitions.meaning: to say or voice words aloud
complete, total, as in a total disaster

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to say something; the adjective means absolute or complete.

clue.text: Very legal tout

parts.note: very means so, as in so good
licit means lawful, legal

explanation.surface: A remark that touting is perfectly lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: To tout is to drum up business or custom by approaching people directly.

clue.text: Americans heading west look for denial

indicators.note: heading west in an across clue means reading from right to left, backwards

parts.note: to look for something is to seek it
nay is an old word of denial, no

explanation.surface: US travellers going west in search of a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' reverses the whole charade, which suits an across entry read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial name for people from the United States, used especially by outsiders.

clue.text: A bit of skirt that's used to attract attention

parts.note: the hem is the bottom edge of a skirt

explanation.surface: A short skirt worn to catch someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of skirt' is old slang for an attractive woman, but here it is just the hem.
explanation.definitionFit: A small throat-clearing cough is a polite noise made to catch someone's notice.

clue.text: Bigots' hobby, regularly engaging in kinky phone sex

definitions.note: the possessive is read as bigots, plural, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: engaging in means the hobby letters go inside the reworked letters
kinky means twisted, so these letters are rearranged
regularly picks every other letter of the word, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A bigot's pastime turns out to be regular kinky phone calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes OB from hOBby; 'kinky' turns PHONE SEX into XENPHES-style letters, with OB 'engaging in' them.
explanation.definitionFit: People hostile to foreigners are a particular kind of prejudiced, intolerant person.

clue.text: Here xenophobes break out and sleep with Poles outside

definitions.note: the xenophobes clue is numbered thirteen, so this is where that answer sits

indicators.note: break out suggests the letters burst free and land in a new order
outside says the poles go round the sleep word

parts.note: the two poles are south and north, S and N
to doze is to sleep lightly

explanation.surface: Bigots escape a prison here and sleep with Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 13-across: XENOPHOBES is clue 13, and a baker's dozen is thirteen. 'out' rearranges BREAK as BAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker's dozen is thirteen, the number of the clue where those bigots are entered.

clue.text: See 3
Leave computer brand staffing centre

parts.note: a brand's emblem is its logo

indicators.note: the centre of staffing is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: Quitting a computer company whose brand runs the staffing centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a session on a computer system is to sign out, leaving the machine.

clue.text: Ask somehow to be in front or quit

indicators.note: to be in says the rearranged letters go inside the front word

parts.note: fore means front, as in the fore part of a ship

indicators.note: somehow says these letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A request to step to the front or else leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the three letters of 'Ask' as SAK.
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake something is to abandon or desert it, giving it up for good.

clue.text: Why said figurehead is protected by clumsy minder, surely not David!

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded by it, so these letters go inside
clumsy means awkward, so these letters are put in a new order
said tells us the word is taken by its sound, the letter name

parts.note: the word why is pronounced like the letter Y
the head of figure is its first letter, F

explanation.surface: A bodyguard fumbles to protect a figurehead, asking why.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Goliath, and David, who slew Goliath in the Bible, was certainly no pal. 'clumsy' rearranges the minder letters around the two inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of address for a pal, which David in the Bible surely never was to Goliath.

clue.text: Doctor Seuss to underwrite non- standard parody of a legendary traveller

indicators.note: in a down clue, to underwrite is to be written under another piece
non- signals that the standard word is removed

parts.note: par is the standard, as in up to par

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dr Seuss sponsors a parody of a famous wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the title of Dr Seuss but is the anagram signal; 'non-' removes the standard word from the front of 'parody'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero of Homer's Odyssey spent ten years wandering home from Troy.

clue.text: Suspicious about early start, finally wipe lens

indicators.note: about means going round, so the suspicious word wraps the start letter

parts.note: fishy means dubious, suspicious

indicators.note: start picks the first letter of early
finally picks the last letter of wipe

explanation.surface: Wary of an early start, someone gives the lens a final wipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A very wide-angle lens giving a curved, distorted image is called this.

clue.text: Heckled and perhaps rejected: court dismissed

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise
dismissed means the court letters are thrown out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A rejected case is thrown out of court amid jeering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' takes CT out of REJECTED, leaving REJEED, and 'perhaps' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt with taunts, much as a crowd that mocked and booed someone.

clue.text: One and only one in French intelligence superficially usable

parts.note: the French for one is un
IQ is the usual measure of intelligence

indicators.note: superficially takes only the surface letters, the outside ones

explanation.surface: A one-off French intelligence report that is barely usable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal or parallel is the only one of its kind.

clue.text: Slap on the wrist from backbench idealists

indicators.note: from says the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Backbench idealists get a mild reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span 'backbenCH IDEalists'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap on the wrist is a mild rebuke, so as a verb it means to scold.

clue.text: Remarkable theory won't get modified

indicators.note: letters that get modified are altered, here rearranged

explanation.surface: A striking theory that refuses to be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth noting is significant, notable, deserving attention.

clue.text: Poetry's not extremely modest

definitions.note: the 's reads as is, and the plural answer stands for poetry in general

indicators.note: not extremely drops the extreme letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: Poetry described as not especially modest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject, taken together, are a body of verse.

clue.text: See 6
Don providing citation around 9

indicators.note: around means the citation goes round the number

parts.note: a citation is a quote
nine in Roman numerals is IX

explanation.surface: A university don giving a reference to clue 9.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a lecturer, but it is the title of Cervantes's Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote is the deluded knight of Cervantes's novel, whose title is the Spanish honorific.

clue.text: See 7
Perhaps some olive oil, and pizza filling found in Doctor Livingstone's cases

indicators.note: found in says the pizza filling is placed inside the cases
the cases of words are their outside letters
the filling of pizza is everything but its outer letters

explanation.surface: Pizza topped with olive oil, served to the explorer Dr Livingstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Livingstone' looks like one name, but each word supplies its own outer pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin trickle of olive oil poured over food is an example of this cooking term.

clue.text: Start of tropical disease outbreak in part of Manhattan

indicators.note: in puts the start letter inside the rearranged letters
an outbreak breaks the letters up, rearranging them
start of picks the first letter of tropical

explanation.surface: A tropical disease begins to spread through part of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak' rearranges DISEASE as EASSIDE, with T put 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Upper and Lower East Side are districts of New York's Manhattan island.

clue.text: Have you ever noticed anxious students? At first, they laugh

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of each of the six preceding words

explanation.surface: A question about nervous students, who first of all just laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted hyenas are famous for a cackling call that sounds like human laughter.
